hero.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement with 1,162 stops in four weeks
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and is placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said excessive speeding is common in St. Lucie County and that she most recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. He said his top speed stop on Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, was 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155 percent increase.

Del Toro said he has a family that drives on these roadways and cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones, adding that he wants to make the community safer. Residents say the problem is hard to miss. Ashley, a St. Lucie County resident, described what she sees on local roads as insane and said nobody slows down. Jessica, another local driver, said drivers are careless and cut people off.

cards.headline: Donalds and Jolly lead Florida governor's race as primary enters final stretch
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly have emerged as frontrunners in Florida's gubernatorial race as the August 18 primary approaches. Donalds holds a commanding advantage in Republican polling and fundraising, while Jolly has consolidated support in the Democratic contest, though the closing weeks are bringing new attacks, a ballot challenge and questions about the candidates' vulnerabilities heading toward November.

A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48% among Republican voters, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and received an endorsement from President Donald Trump. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins as lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary. Collins used a Thursday campaign call to position himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds, arguing the race is between the two of them despite the polling gap. He also urged Renner to leave the race. Fishback faces two major challenges: a $400,000 attack ad campaign from The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz that characterizes past statements by Fishback as antisemitic, and a ballot eligibility challenge from Collins. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee over allegations that Fishback does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida and has lived in the state throughout his life, purchasing a Washington condo only to visit his parents.

On the Democratic side, Jolly addressed his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni, who federal prosecutors allege stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit managing trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs. The alleged scheme operated from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Govoni supported Jolly's past political campaigns and served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft and welcomed scrutiny of his record. "Unlike too many politicians today who hide behind lawyers or refuse to answer questions, I'm an open book," Jolly said. "Because when you've done nothing wrong, you have nothing to hide."

A June Change Research survey commissioned by Freedom Project USA, a group aligned with Democrats, showed Jolly leading Donalds 47% to 42% among registered voters and 49% to 43% among likely voters. However, respondents were shown prepared descriptions of both candidates before being asked whom they supported, making the results less directly comparable to a standard ballot test. Florida's voter registration deadline is July 20, with early voting required from August 15 and the primary set for August 18.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition begins in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.body:
Demolition crews are tearing down damaged buildings at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a complete overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said the school was already scheduled for construction when the hurricane hit. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," Gernaine said. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on."

Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out.

The Martin County School District hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027. The district emphasized that safety measures are in place to protect students while construction proceeds on campus.

cards.headline: JetBlue ends Vero Beach to New York JFK route after nine months, citing low demand
cards.teaser: JetBlue is ending direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport on Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating in December.
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating. "Demand for this new route has not materialized as we had hoped," JetBlue said in a statement to WPTV. The airline will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a "game changer" for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

cards.headline: Miami Heat introduce Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis Jr. at Kaseya Center
cards.teaser: The Miami Heat introduced two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo and forward Bobby Portis Jr. on Thursday afternoon to loud chants at Kaseya Center.
cards.body:
Loud chants of "Giannis" filled the Kaseya Center on Thursday afternoon as the Miami Heat introduced their newest stars. Head Coach Erik Spoelstra said Pat Riley asked him if he wanted to coach Giannis, and he said yes. Spoelstra called it a no-brainer to coach a two-time MVP, NBA champion, Finals MVP and more. Antetokounmpo, standing 6 feet 11 inches and weighing 240 pounds, said he thrives on pressure and needs it at this point in his career to go to the next level. He said he had to get out of his comfort zone. Coming off back-to-back injury-filled seasons, Antetokounmpo said he feels like whenever he puts his mind to something, he usually accomplishes it, and this is the best route for him to win more championships.

Bobby Portis Jr. was also introduced on Thursday. Portis said he prides himself on working every day in the summer to get better and has been coming off the bench his whole career as a sixth man type of guy. He said being aggressive is what he has always been. Portis said he has been playing with Giannis for six years now, going on seven, and it has been real fun. He said his relationship with Bam Adebayo was built off of being competitors. Spoelstra said the squad with Antetokounmpo, Portis and Adebayo will play a lot of positionless ball. Antetokounmpo said the moment he is coached hard, everyone else is going to follow, adding he does not want it to be sugar-coated and needs the truth so he can apply that to the game.

cards.headline: Ballot challenge threatens to exclude votes for Florida gubernatorial candidate Fishback
cards.teaser: A hearing beginning July 21 will determine whether businessman James Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor.
cards.body:
Lt. Gov. Jay Collins is challenging James Fishback's candidacy for governor, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots.

Fishback is also facing a $400,000 ad campaign from The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Fishback at 8% in the Republican primary, behind frontrunner Byron Donalds at 48% and Collins at 9%. Paul Renner received 4%, with about 26% of respondents remaining undecided.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks foster families during shelter renovation
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. The renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said these animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction. It's very loud and the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal, she said. About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance lowers rates 5.6% for Florida homeowners, adds disappearing deductible
cards.teaser: Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings the company is required to pass along to customers, and they have been.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, the deductible goes down 20 percent each year as long as the customer does not have a loss. Once a customer has a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292.

hero.headline: Lantana Finland House celebrates Panthers' four Finnish stars
hero.teaser: The Finland Club in Lantana has become a hockey hotspot thanks to four Finnish players on the Florida Panthers roster, including captain Aleksander Barkov.
hero.body:
The Finland House, called Suomi Talo in Finnish, is located on Finlandia Boulevard in Lantana and serves as headquarters for some of South Florida's most passionate Panthers fans. The Finland Club has been celebrating Finnish culture in Palm Beach County for 80 years. Inside, walls are lined with pictures and crests representing every town and city across Finland. According to a longtime member who gave WPTV Anchor and Panthers 360 host Mike Trim a tour, the Finns came with Flagler to build The Breakers and then shipped back to Lake Worth in the evenings.

The Panthers roster includes four Finnish players who have become local heroes: Captain Aleksander Barkov, Anton Lundell, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen. All four played crucial roles in the Panthers' two Stanley Cup championships. Last June, Barkov and Lundell captured gold for Finland at the World Hockey Championship. Club member Jorma Olsson recalled that they called all the Finns Sunday morning and the whole place was packed. When Lundell scored the overtime goal, the president was afraid they were going to lose the roof. Club member Jyrki Koiveharju said having these Finnish players on the Panthers warms his heart and is extremely important to the community. The Panthers hold an annual Finnish Heritage Night at Amerant Bank Arena, with fans flying all the way from Finland in previous years just to attend that special game.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts qualify for Junior Olympics with top 15 national finish
cards.teaser: Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee, and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month.
cards.body:
Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine from Flip City Gym and Cheer competed at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and secured a top 15 finish. The trio came close to a perfect score during the competition, earning a 9.9 on one event. Head Coach Candice Lazuka said getting a perfect 10 is difficult, making their near-perfect score significant.

The three gymnasts had a strong season leading up to nationals. They competed locally and traveled to other competitions before advancing to states and regionals, according to Lazuka. Each gymnast came to the sport for different reasons, with Rose-Daris saying it started because she knew how to do a cartwheel, Supan inspired by gymnasts she saw on YouTube, and Rine simply loving to learn new things.

The top 15 finish qualified the team for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Rose-Daris said she is excited to travel to an entirely different part of the world, while Supan described the opportunity as happy and exciting. Rine has a specific goal for the competition, saying she wants to get first place on floors.

cards.headline: Florida Panthers to open 2026-27 season on road before home opener against Minnesota Wild
cards.teaser: The Panthers will start their regular season campaign on the road against four Western Conference opponents before returning to Amerant Bank Arena on Oct. 11.
cards.body:
The Florida Panthers will begin their 2026-27 NHL regular season on the road, opening against the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on Sept. 29 in what will be a marquee matchup to begin the year. The road trip continues with a stop in San Jose on Oct. 6 as part of a four-game road swing against Western Conference opponents. After completing the road trip, the Panthers will return to South Florida for their highly anticipated home opener on Saturday, Oct. 11 when they welcome the Minnesota Wild to Amerant Bank Arena.

December will be particularly busy with seven home games, including four special holiday matchups to close out 2026. The Panthers will host the Buffalo Sabres on Dec. 28. Fans will enjoy two consecutive five-game homestands during the season, with the first running from Dec. 19-30 and the second from March 2-12.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two late goals to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday, advancing to the World Cup final where they will face Spain on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina rallied for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez. Anthony Gordon scored the opening goal for England in the 55th minute. Martinez told reporters he dreamed it and told Alexis Mac Allister that he was going to come on and win it. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina attacks mounted. Messi fed the ball to Fernandez to sweep in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for Martinez to head in the winner. At the final whistle, Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief.

The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk, more rhythm and the feeling that they have nothing to lose anymore, which freed them up and held England back because they played with a feeling that they have a lot to lose. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team is unique and they're going to try to win and leave everything out there. Messi, now 39 and likely playing at his last World Cup, is one win away from further strengthening his case to be considered the greatest soccer player of all time.

cards.headline: Spain defeats France 2-0 to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro scored as Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010 with a 2-0 victory over France on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot after a play by teenager Lamine Yamal, Pedro Porro added another goal and Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010 with a 2-0 victory over France on Tuesday. A day after his 19th birthday, Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne in the penalty area in the 22nd minute. After a poor first touch with his head, Digne was trying to clear the ball when Yamal raced in from behind to challenge. The ball hit off the elbow of the leaping teen before he was kicked by Digne, playing in his 63rd game for France only six days before his 33rd birthday. Oyarzabal's fifth goal of this year's World Cup marked the first time either team has trailed in their seven games in this tournament. Porro's give-and-go with Dani Olmo in the 58th minute put Spain up 2-0. Yamal was denied a goal on a close offside call that came soon after.

Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. They face each other on Wednesday in Atlanta. France, FIFA's top-ranked team, was trying to become only the third team to reach three consecutive World Cup finals. They instead will play in the third-place game in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Saturday, the day before the final at MetLife Stadium. This marked the third summer in a row that Spain beat France in a tournament semifinal match.

cards.headline: Okeeheelee All-Stars make history with scoreless run, head to Southeast Regionals
cards.body:
The Okeeheelee Comanches 10U All-Stars have accomplished something unprecedented in their program's history, allowing zero runs during district and state tournament play. The streak began in May during district play, where the Comanches scored 49 runs while shutting out all opponents. In June, the team traveled to Auburndale to compete against the top 17 teams in the state tournament. They went undefeated, scoring 39 runs while maintaining their scoreless defensive record. "It's super cool because we've let up zero runs this season. It's like the first time it's happened in Okeeheelee history," said 10U all-star Tate Krass. This marks the first time in Okeeheelee history that a team has given up zero runs in this span.

The success came after early setbacks this summer, when the team lost tournaments they felt they should have won. "There have been games that have been really close games, like championship games and semifinal games, where maybe we felt like we were the better team and should win it, and we don't," said head coach Jose Espinosa. He uses those moments as teaching opportunities. "I don't really coach baseball; I coach life through baseball. For us, it's teaching all those things, accountability and how to work together. For us, it's about making sure that when they do make mistakes, they do know how to respond to that," Espinosa said. The team arrived in North Carolina this week to represent Florida in the Cal Ripken Southeast Regional Tournament. If successful, they will advance to the Cal Ripken World Series.

hero.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa discounts
hero.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August. The mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses.
hero.body:
Downtown Delray Beach is encouraging residents and visitors to prioritize health and self-care this summer through a new Wellness Pass featuring free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the city's downtown district. The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August.

According to the DDA, the mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach. The pass does not require an app download. Miller Physical Therapy is participating with wellness-related services and promotions. The program arrives as wellness tourism and fitness-focused experiences continue to grow in popularity across South Florida.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free promotion through August 10
cards.teaser: The zoo's popular Kids Free promotion has now been extended through Aug. 10. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Zoo is extending its Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission.

The zoo also announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include Paws & Santa Claus in July, Tails & Touchdowns in August and Decades After Dark in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback.

The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and now has a name: Bonza. That's Aussie slang for awesome or excellent, Joiner said. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

cards.headline: Vero Beach museum reopens with history exhibits
cards.teaser: A museum in Vero Beach has reopened with history exhibits for visitors.
cards.body: A museum in Vero Beach has reopened and is now displaying history exhibits for the public. The reopening provides Indian River County residents and visitors with access to historical collections and educational programming.

cards.headline: John Brewster Music performs Thankful Thursdays at Hudsons on Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: John Brewster Music is performing at Thankful Thursdays at Hudsons, offering live music entertainment for Treasure Coast residents.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to children at 35 summer sites
cards.teaser: The nonprofit in Lake Worth Beach supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children while school is out.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is helping provide thousands of free meals to children this summer through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program, according to Food Bank leaders. The nonprofit organization said it supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children while school is out for the summer. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, the organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone.

During a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV, Palm Beach County Food Bank CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county. Chef Doug Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. The loading dock operation featured drivers and volunteers preparing for morning deliveries to Summer BreakSpot sites throughout Palm Beach County. The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach.

hero.headline: Donalds and Jolly lead Florida governor's race as primary enters final stretch
hero.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly have emerged as frontrunners in Florida's gubernatorial race as the August 18 primary approaches. Donalds holds a commanding advantage in Republican polling and fundraising, while Jolly has consolidated support in the Democratic contest, though the closing weeks are bringing new attacks, a ballot challenge and questions about the candidates' vulnerabilities heading toward November.

A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48% among Republican voters, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and received an endorsement from President Donald Trump. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins as lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary. Collins used a Thursday campaign call to position himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds, arguing the race is between the two of them despite the polling gap. He also urged Renner to leave the race. Fishback faces two major challenges: a $400,000 attack ad campaign from The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz that characterizes past statements by Fishback as antisemitic, and a ballot eligibility challenge from Collins. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee over allegations that Fishback does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida and has lived in the state throughout his life, purchasing a Washington condo only to visit his parents.

On the Democratic side, Jolly addressed his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni, who federal prosecutors allege stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit managing trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs. The alleged scheme operated from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Govoni supported Jolly's past political campaigns and served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft and welcomed scrutiny of his record. "Unlike too many politicians today who hide behind lawyers or refuse to answer questions, I'm an open book," Jolly said. "Because when you've done nothing wrong, you have nothing to hide."

A June Change Research survey commissioned by Freedom Project USA, a group aligned with Democrats, showed Jolly leading Donalds 47% to 42% among registered voters and 49% to 43% among likely voters. However, respondents were shown prepared descriptions of both candidates before being asked whom they supported, making the results less directly comparable to a standard ballot test. Florida's voter registration deadline is July 20, with early voting required from August 15 and the primary set for August 18.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance cuts Florida homeowners rates by 5.6%
cards.teaser: The Ormond Beach-based insurer announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible program as companies cite reduced lawsuits from state reforms.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said their customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings the company is required to pass along to customers, and they have been.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as a customer doesn't have a loss. Once a customer has a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Premiums in South Florida generally run high, and online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

cards.headline: Ballot challenge threatens to exclude votes for Florida gubernatorial candidate Fishback
cards.teaser: A hearing beginning July 21 will determine whether businessman James Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor.
cards.body:
Lt. Gov. Jay Collins is challenging James Fishback's candidacy for governor, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots.

Fishback is also facing a $400,000 ad campaign from The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Fishback at 8% in the Republican primary, behind frontrunner Byron Donalds at 48% and Collins at 9%. Paul Renner received 4%, with about 26% of respondents remaining undecided.

cards.headline: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jolly addresses ties to indicted Clearwater financier
cards.teaser: David Jolly responded to questions about his past business and political relationship with Leo Govoni, who federal prosecutors allege stole more than $100 million.
cards.body:
Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025 and involved fraudulent account statements and transfers through Govoni-controlled companies. Govoni and Witeck have been charged. Jolly is not a defendant in the case.

Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Govoni also supported Jolly's past political campaigns and served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. Donalds supporters have circulated opposition research emphasizing those connections, noting that Jolly and his wife worked for Govoni-linked companies, Govoni raised money for Jolly's campaigns, and Jolly later employed Govoni's son in Congress. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft and welcomed scrutiny of his record. Jolly said that unlike too many politicians today who hide behind lawyers or refuse to answer questions, he is an open book because when you have done nothing wrong, you have nothing to hide.

cards.teaser: The governor has not endorsed Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, whom he appointed in August 2025, or any other candidate in the race.

President Donald Trump has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds in the race. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48%, followed by Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds also holds a major financial advantage, with his campaign announcing more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation.

Collins used a Thursday campaign call to position himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds, despite trailing the congressman in polling, money and endorsements. Collins defended his support for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and law enforcement, rejected claims of tension between his campaign and staff inside the governor's office, and urged Renner to leave the race. He also argued Donalds could struggle in a general election. Collins said the race is between Donalds and himself and that his campaign has a clear path. Recent reports placed Collins' available resources at a fraction of Donalds' amount.

hero.headline: Palm City WPTV Weather Spotter with Navy background discusses decades of forecasting evolution
hero.teaser: A Palm City WPTV Weather Spotter with a lifelong passion for meteorology spoke with WPTV First Alert Weather Meteorologist James Wieland about how weather forecasting has evolved over the decades.
hero.body:
Brian Botley served in the Navy, where mapping the weather was part of his duties. His interest in weather began as a child in Oakland Park, where he moved in 1951. Botley said his dad was always plotting the hurricanes, which sparked his interest. He went in the Navy and was picked to go to the Aerographer's Mate School in Lakehurst. His first job was plotting weather maps. They had some satellites starting in 1961 or 1962, but it wasn't the coverage they have now. Botley compared the early satellite technology to 1953 radar.

WPTV First Alert Weather Meteorologist James Wieland showed Botley the technology used in today's weather coverage and walked him through how computer models and modern radar systems have transformed forecasting. Botley said joining WPTV's Weather Spotter program felt like a natural extension of something he was already doing on his own. He does this all the time just on his own and said it may be fun because there are other people there.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff intensifies traffic enforcement with summer crackdown on speeding
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative this summer to reduce speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern. He said he has a family that drives on these roadways and wants to make the community safer.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding, noting that she recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, which has a 25 mph speed limit, Rodrigues recorded a top speed of 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

Residents say the dangerous driving is hard to miss. Ashley, a St. Lucie County resident, described what she sees on local roads as insane and said nobody slows down. Jessica, another local driver, said drivers are careless and cut people off. Del Toro emphasized the personal nature of his commitment to safer roads, saying he cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones and wants to make the community safer.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
cards.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
cards.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: JetBlue ends direct flights from Vero Beach to New York JFK after nine months, citing low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue stated that demand for the new route has not materialized as hoped, though the airline will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. Despite the initial optimism surrounding the launch, the route failed to attract sufficient passenger numbers to remain viable for the airline.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The airport's efforts to grow its flight offerings aimed to provide more convenient options for residents and visitors to the Treasure Coast region. The continuation of the Boston service suggests JetBlue still sees some value in maintaining a presence at the smaller regional airport.

JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline's decision to end the JFK route comes as carriers across the industry continue evaluating route performance and adjusting their networks based on demand patterns.
